acceptance_oracle: For supported discovery operation kinds, terminal JSON records may include only an explicit source identifier persisted in the operation parameters: DISCOVER.source_id, COMPANY_DISCOVER.monitoring_source_id, or COMPANY_SOURCE_REFRESH.source_id. The identifier must pass the existing fixed identifier syntax and must not contain credential markers. Logging remains after durable terminal-state persistence; params, candidate fields, URLs, secrets, and arbitrary payload values are never serialized.
implementation: Added a discovery-kind allowlist mapping persisted source identifier fields to the source_id log field.
Malformed values and identifiers containing API key, access key/token, secret, token, password, or credential markers are omitted.

Unit tests cover all three supported discovery mappings and missing, URL-shaped, and secret-shaped values; the existing PREPARE privacy test confirms discovery context is not emitted for PREPARE operations.
The worker lifecycle test persists a DISCOVER operation with a source_id, executes the worker, and verifies the completed durable state and corresponding terminal log record.

test_first.observed: With the production enrichment temporarily absent, the test failed its source_id assertion: None != 'source-123'. The implementation was restored and the same behavior passed in the final focused run.

validation.skip_detail: PostgreSQLWorkerCrashRecoveryTests skipped because MJOBS_WORKER_RECOVERY_POSTGRES_URL is unset.

environment.database: Temporary SQLite databases in unit/integration tests

limitations: This scoped improvement exposes only a persisted source identifier. It does not infer source provider, ATS, job, posting, or additional company attributes from candidate input or worker results.
Posting and ATS context are not available as safe identifiers on the terminal operation rows/params covered by this slice; remaining MJ-REQ-177 context is incomplete and the issue remains PARTIAL.
The optional PostgreSQL worker recovery class and the full Python suite were NOT_RUN; no live Redis/RQ service was used.
GitHub-hosted checks remain NOT_RUN under local-only policy.
